title.en: Synchronized orthogonal slices with one probe point

summary: Coordinate three slice planes and a 3D locator through one authoritative source-space point.
objective: Show three orthogonal slices and a 3D locator; moving a probe in any view must identify the same source location in every view.
intent_signals: Show three orthogonal slices and a 3D locator; moving a probe in any view must identify the same source location in every view.
example_prompts: Show three orthogonal slices and a 3D locator; moving a probe in any view must identify the same source location in every view.

principles: Use a shared probe point to answer where a feature lies across sections; merely placing three slice images side by side does not establish correspondence.
Declare source axis convention, voxel-to-model mapping and which properties are linked. Share coordinates without assuming that three plane orientations should become identical.
implementation: Keep dataset revision, source-space probe, plane basis and time index in one state owner. A drag maps viewport coordinates through that view plane into source space, then commits once; derive all other crosshairs and offsets from the resulting point.

For an orthogonal mode keep plane normals mutually perpendicular in the declared model frame. For oblique acquisition, distinguish source index axes from anatomical/world axes; do not silently label index-aligned planes anatomical.

Use the same volume, time and declared interpolation policy for corresponding scalar samples. Label discrete segmentation sampling separately; clamp a probe only with visible feedback, or show an out-of-bounds state.
Offer link toggles with explicit scope, numeric point entry and reset for probe/orientation. A shared cursor does not require all zoom, pan and legend controls to be shared.
observable_checks: Use a labeled synthetic anisotropic volume with known orientation. Select one landmark in each view in turn: source coordinates, time index and 3D locator agree after the declared transform.
Pan or resize one viewport without moving the probe: its reported source coordinate remains fixed. Switch interpolation and verify the disclosure changes with it.
Move outside the data extent and return, then reset; no stale crosshair or accidental recursion leaves one view on the previous point.

known_limits: Requires known spatial transforms and registration when multiple datasets are compared. Linked views do not perform registration, segmentation or diagnosis.
Draft authored guidance; no renderer, interaction artifact or scientific result was executed for this record.
creative_affordances: Choose layout and visual emphasis to support the stated inspection task; these are design proposals rather than proven usability improvements.

claims.statement: Slicer documents linked slice-view groups, synchronization of selected display properties, and a crosshair action shared across views; center synchronization is specifically described for parallel views.
claims.scope: Slicer documented UI behavior; the proposed source-space state owner and orthogonal-view contract are authored.
